userStories.title: features resolve reports config errors and adopts the run's profile
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make features resolve distinguish acceptance-resolution errors from absent PRDs and use the run profile chain.

**Motivation** — `resolveFeatureAcceptance` (`packages/nax/src/cli/features-acceptance.ts`) catches every error, including `CONFIG_SCHEMA_INVALID` from `loadConfig`, and returns `status: "no-prd"`.

**Approach** — Part A — features resolve (US-001)

### Integration

This part changes two signatures. The baseline is stated only to locate the code; it is never the interface to implement.

**`AcceptanceResolutionStatus` / `AcceptanceResolution`** — `src/cli/features-acceptance.ts:37` (US-001)
- Baseline: `type AcceptanceResolutionStatus = "ok" | "disabled" | "no-prd"`; `AcceptanceResolution { status; enabled; groups }`.
- Target:
  ```typescript
  export type AcceptanceResolutionStatus = "ok" | "disabled" | "no-prd" | "error";
  export interface AcceptanceResolutionError {
    /** NaxError code when the thrown error is a NaxError (e.g. "CONFIG_SCHEMA_INVALID"), else "UNKNOWN". */
    code: string;
    /** errorMessage(err) of the caught error. */
    message: string;
  }
  export interface AcceptanceResolution {
    status: AcceptanceResolutionStatus;
    enabled: boolean;
    groups: AcceptanceGroupResult[];
    /** Present only when status === "error". */
    error?: AcceptanceResolutionError;
  }
  ```

**`resolveFeatureAcceptance`** — `src/cli/features-acceptance.ts:56` (US-001)
- Baseline: `resolveFeatureAcceptance(featureName: string, workdir: string): Promise<AcceptanceResolution>`.
- Target: `resolveFeatureAcceptance(featureName: string, workdir: string, configOverrides?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<AcceptanceResolution>` — `configOverrides` is passed as the second argument of `loadConfig(workdir, configOverrides)`.

**`resolveFeatureSpec`** — `src/cli/features-resolve.ts` (US-001)
- Baseline: `resolveFeatureSpec(name: string | undefined, workdir: string): Promise<ResolveResult>`.
- Target: `resolveFeatureSpec(name: string | undefined, workdir: string, opts?: { profile?: string[]; envProfile?: string }): Promise<ResolveResult>`. `opts.envProfile` defaults to `process.env.NAX_PROFILE`. For a resolved feature it computes the profile chain once with `resolveRunProfileOverride({ prdPath: join(featureDir(repoRoot, name), "prd.json"), projectRoot: workdir, cliProfile: opts.profile, envProfile })` (`featureDir` is the helper at `src/config/paths/index.ts:119`) and, when the chain is non-empty, passes `{ profile: chain }` as the config overrides to both `resolveFeatureAcceptance` and the module-private `resolveTestPatterns`.

Read, not changed: `resolveRunProfileOverride` (`src/cli/resolve-run-profile.ts:21`, precedence CLI `--profile` > `NAX_PROFILE` > PRD `routingProfile`), `loadConfig(startDir?, cliOverrides?)` (`src/config/loader.ts:294`), `collectProfile` (`bin/nax.ts:139`), `NaxError.code`.

### Status rules (ordered; first match wins)

| Condition | status | error |
|:---|:---|:---|
| No `.nax/` dir found from `workdir` | `no-prd` | absent |
| `loadConfig` throws | `error` | `{ code, message }` of the thrown error |
| `acceptance.enabled` resolves `false` | `disabled` | absent |
| `<naxDir>/features/<name>/prd.json` does not exist | `no-prd` | absent |
| `loadPRD`, grouping or command resolution throws | `error` | `{ code, message }` of the thrown error |
| otherwise | `ok` | absent |

`resolveFeatureAcceptance` still never throws. The existing `warn` log on a caught error stays.

### CLI Behavior

`nax features resolve [name]` gains `--profile <name>` (comma-separated or repeated, using `collectProfile`, same as `run`/`plan`). The command's exit codes and stdout/stderr split are unchanged: exit 0 when `result.status === "ok"`, 1 on hard error or `not-a-nax-repo`, 2 otherwise; the JSON document goes to stdout. An `acceptance.status` of `"error"` does not change the exit code (the top-level `status` still decides it).

**Scope** — In: acceptance status/type changes, optional overrides, both named and auto-discovered feature resolution, CLI profile option and associated regression tests. Replace the existing malformed-PRD and invalid/legacy-config tests that assert no-prd with error/groups-empty/never-throw expectations. Out: US-002 MCP locks, US-003 pre-run steps, US-004/US-005 cost query and command. The finish flow is unchanged: an acceptance status of `"error"` arrives with `groups: []`, so `finish/route.ts` routes it as `unverified` (fail-closed); surfacing `error.message` in the finish stop reason is a follow-up. Profile-awareness is added to `nax features resolve` only; other commands that call `loadConfig` without a profile are unchanged.

**Interface** — Target TypeScript signatures (not the baselines):
```typescript
resolveFeatureAcceptance(featureName: string, workdir: string, configOverrides?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<AcceptanceResolution>
resolveFeatureSpec(name: string | undefined, workdir: string, opts?: { profile?: string[]; envProfile?: string }): Promise<ResolveResult>
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance("feat", workdir) returns status: "error" when the project .nax/config.json fails schema validation (execution.storyIsolation: "bogus") and prd.json exists.

[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance("feat", workdir) returns error.code equal to "CONFIG_SCHEMA_INVALID" when prd.json exists and .nax/config.json fails schema validation with execution.storyIsolation: "bogus".

[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance("feat", workdir) returns error.message containing "Invalid configuration" when prd.json exists and .nax/config.json fails schema validation with execution.storyIsolation: "bogus".
[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance returns status: "error" with groups: [] when prd.json exists but is not valid JSON, and never throws.
[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance returns status: "no-prd" with no error property when the config is valid and prd.json does not exist.
[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance returns no error property on an ok result.

[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance("feat", workdir, { profile: ["fix"] }) returns status: "ok" when the project config is invalid on its own but valid once the project profile .nax/profiles/fix.json is overlaid.

[unit] resolveFeatureSpec("feat", workdir) returns acceptance.status: "ok" when the config is invalid on its own, the PRD's routingProfile is "fix", .nax/profiles/fix.json makes it valid, and envProfile is unset.
[unit] resolveFeatureSpec("feat", workdir, { profile: ["fix"] }) returns acceptance.status: "ok" when the PRD has no routingProfile and the config is valid only under fix.

[unit] With process.env.NAX_PROFILE set to "other" (restored after the test) and a project profile .nax/profiles/other.json that leaves the config invalid, resolveFeatureSpec("feat", workdir) (no opts, so envProfile defaults to the env value) does not adopt the PRD's routingProfile "fix", so acceptance.status is "error".
[unit] resolveFeatureSpec("feat", workdir) returns a defined testPatterns when the config is invalid on its own and the PRD's routingProfile "fix" makes it valid.
[cli] nax features resolve feat --json -d <dir> exits with code 0 when the spec resolves and acceptance.status is "error" (invalid config, no profile).

[cli] nax features resolve feat --json --profile fix -d <dir> prints a JSON document whose acceptance.status is "ok" for a project whose config is valid only under fix and whose PRD has no routingProfile.
[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance returns status: "no-prd" with no error property when no .nax/ directory is found from workdir.
[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance returns status: "disabled" with no error property when the loaded config resolves acceptance.enabled to false, even when prd.json is absent.
[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance returns status: "error" with the caught code and message when loadConfig throws, even when prd.json is absent.
[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance returns status: "error" with groups: [] and the caught error's code and message when loadPRD, grouping or command resolution throws, without propagating the error.
[unit] resolveFeatureAcceptance returns status: "error" with error.message naming the cause and groups: [] when the config is invalid/legacy, and never throws.

routing.reasoning: Bounded resolver and CLI changes reuse the existing profile helper; update the two old catch-all regression expectations and test precedence before implementation.

suggestedCriteria: resolveFeatureAcceptance returns error.code equal to "UNKNOWN" when a caught error is not a NaxError.
resolveFeatureSpec(undefined, workdir) adopts the sole discovered feature's PRD routingProfile for both acceptance and testPatterns.
nax features resolve feat --json --profile base,fix and --profile base --profile fix resolve the same ordered profile chain.

modifiedFiles.reason: two tests pin the old catch-all. (1) "returns status=no-prd when prd.json is malformed (never throws)" (`:106`) asserts `status` `no-prd` for an unparseable PRD file; replacing invariant: a malformed PRD file resolves to `status: "error"`, `groups: []`, and never throws. (2) "degrades to no-prd (never throws) when the config is invalid/legacy" (`:118`) asserts `status` `no-prd` when `loadConfig` throws; replacing invariant: an invalid/legacy config resolves to `status: "error"` with `error.message` naming the cause, `groups: []`, and never throws.
the `features resolve` command gains `.option("--profile <name>", ..., collectProfile, [])` and passes `{ profile: options.profile }` to `resolveFeatureSpec`.

userStories.title: Global MCP lock fallback
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve a global MCP lock only when a project lock is absent, and expose the deciding lock source.

**Motivation** — A user who defines MCP servers once in `~/.nax/config.json` must lock and commit in every project; a lock under `~/.nax/` is ignored, and a project with no lock withholds every tool.

**Approach** — Part B — global MCP lock (US-002)

### Integration

**`McpWithheldEntry`** — `src/mcp/provider.ts:24` (US-002)
- Baseline: `{ serverId: string; name: string; reason: string }`.
- Target: adds `readonly lockSource: "project" | "global" | "none"` — which lock decided the withholding (`"none"` when no lock resolved).

**`createMcpProviders` default lock read** — `src/mcp/provider.ts:46` (US-002)
- Baseline: `const read = args.readLock ?? readMcpLock;`
- Target: `const read = args.readLock ?? resolveMcpLock;` The `readLock` seam keeps its type `(projectRoot: string) => Promise<McpLockFile | undefined>`. The provider derives `lockSource` from the resolved value: `undefined` → `"none"`; a value carrying `source` → that source; a value without `source` (a test stub returning a bare `McpLockFile`) → `"project"`.

**`runMcpLockCommand`** — `src/cli/mcp.ts:17` (US-002)
- Baseline: `runMcpLockCommand(workdir: string): Promise<void>` writes `<workdir>/.nax/mcp-lock.json`.
- Target: `runMcpLockCommand(workdir: string, opts?: { global?: boolean }): Promise<void>`; with `opts.global === true` it writes through `writeMcpLockAt(globalMcpLockPath(), lock)` instead and prints `Wrote <that path>`.

**`writeMcpLock`** — `src/mcp/lock.ts:61` (US-002)
- Baseline: `writeMcpLock(projectRoot, lock)` sorts and writes `join(projectRoot, ".nax", "mcp-lock.json")`.
- Target: the sort-and-serialise body moves into a new `writeMcpLockAt(path: string, lock: McpLockFile): Promise<void>` (creates the parent dir, writes only `version` and `servers`); `writeMcpLock(projectRoot, lock)` keeps its signature and delegates with `writeMcpLockAt(mcpLockPath(projectRoot), lock)`.

**`nax mcp lock` command** — `bin/nax.ts:992-999` (US-002)
- Baseline: `mcpCmd.command("lock")` with no options; action calls `runMcpLockCommand(process.cwd())` after `runTrustGate(process.cwd())`.
- Target: adds `.option("--global", "Write the lock to the global config dir instead of the project", false)`; the action passes `{ global: options.global === true }`. `runTrustGate` is unchanged.

New in `src/mcp/lock.ts` (exported through the `@/mcp` barrel):

```typescript
export interface ResolvedMcpLock extends McpLockFile {
  /** Which file the lock was read from. Never written to disk. */
  readonly source: "project" | "global";
}
/** <globalDir>/mcp-lock.json; globalDir defaults to globalConfigDir(). */
export function globalMcpLockPath(globalDir?: string): string;
/**
 * Project lock fully overrides the global lock:
 *  1. If <projectRoot>/.nax/mcp-lock.json EXISTS, parse it with readMcpLock's validation.
 *     Valid -> { ...lock, source: "project" }. Malformed -> undefined (fail closed; the
 *     global lock is NOT consulted).
 *  2. Otherwise parse globalMcpLockPath(globalDir). Valid -> { ...lock, source: "global" };
 *     missing or malformed -> undefined.
 */
export async function resolveMcpLock(projectRoot: string, globalDir?: string): Promise<ResolvedMcpLock | undefined>;
```

`writeMcpLockAt` (and so `writeMcpLock`) never writes a `source` field: it serialises only `version` and `servers`. A lock is keyed by server id only: a global lock entry for id `memory` applies to whichever server is configured under `memory` in a project with no project lock (see Out of Scope). The `[provider] <id>__<tool> withheld` warn log gains a `lockSource` field. The rollup (`buildMcpRollup`) carries `withheld` entries through unchanged, so each rollup entry now includes `lockSource`.

`globalConfigDir()` honours `NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR` (`src/config/paths/index.ts:63`), which tests use to point at a temp dir.

### CLI Behavior

`nax mcp lock --global` — same trust gate and same server listing as today; writes the global lock path. Exit codes unchanged (0 on success; thrown errors surface as today).

**Scope** — In: lock resolver/path/writer, provider default reader and attribution, command destination selection, exact withheld assertions and typed rollup fixtures, default-reader integration and trusted CLI tests. Update `test/unit/mcp/provider.test.ts`'s bare-lock expectation to include `lockSource: "project"`; both `test/unit/mcp/rollup.test.ts` withheld literals gain that field while pass-through stays unchanged. Out: US-001 feature profiles, US-003 pre-run setup, US-004/US-005 cost features. Merging the project and global MCP locks per server id is not supported; a present project lock fully overrides the global lock. A global MCP lock is keyed by server id only and is not restricted to servers defined in the global config layer; this is accepted because a project lock fully overrides it and the MCP server spawn still requires project trust.

**Interface** — Additional target signatures:
```typescript
export function writeMcpLockAt(path: string, lock: McpLockFile): Promise<void>;
runMcpLockCommand(workdir: string, opts?: { global?: boolean }): Promise<void>
```
The existing `readLock?: (projectRoot: string) => Promise<McpLockFile | undefined>` seam remains compatible with bare lock stubs. SEAM-3 is verified by constructing providers with no readLock override, not merely by testing resolveMcpLock in isolation.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] resolveMcpLock(projectRoot, globalDir) returns the project lock with source: "project" when <projectRoot>/.nax/mcp-lock.json is valid, even when a valid global lock also exists.
[unit] resolveMcpLock(projectRoot, globalDir) returns the global lock with source: "global" when no project lock file exists and <globalDir>/mcp-lock.json is valid.
[unit] resolveMcpLock returns undefined when the project lock file exists but is malformed, even when a valid global lock exists.
[unit] resolveMcpLock returns undefined when no project lock exists and the global lock is malformed.
[unit] resolveMcpLock returns undefined when neither lock file exists.
[unit] globalMcpLockPath() returns join(globalConfigDir(), "mcp-lock.json"), honouring NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR.

[integration] With NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR pointing at a temp dir whose mcp-lock.json pins tool search_graph for server memory, and a project root with no lock, createMcpProviders built without a readLock override admits search_graph from a pool that advertises it.
[integration] In that same setup, a tool delete_project advertised by the pool but absent from the global lock is reported to onWithheld with lockSource: "global".
[unit] A provider whose lock resolves to undefined reports each withheld tool to onWithheld with lockSource: "none".
[unit] The [provider] <id>__<tool> withheld warn log carries a lockSource field equal to the withheld entry's lockSource.
[integration] runMcpLockCommand(workdir, { global: true }), with one enabled server backed by the fake MCP server fixture test/fixtures/mcp/fake-server.ts, writes the lock to globalMcpLockPath().
[integration] In that same runMcpLockCommand(workdir, { global: true }) setup, <workdir>/.nax/mcp-lock.json is not created.
[unit] writeMcpLockAt(path, lock) output never contains a source key when given a ResolvedMcpLock.
[cli] nax mcp lock --global, run in a trusted temp project with NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR pointing at a temp dir and a stub MCP server configured, writes <globalDir>/mcp-lock.json.
[cli] In that same trusted nax mcp lock --global setup, <cwd>/.nax/mcp-lock.json is not created.

[unit] A provider whose readLock stub returns a bare McpLockFile reports the existing absent-from-lock entry through onWithheld with the same serverId, name and reason plus lockSource: "project", preserving the readLock seam's existing return type.
[unit] writeMcpLock(projectRoot, lock) produces the same key-sorted version-and-servers JSON with a trailing newline at <projectRoot>/.nax/mcp-lock.json as before the writeMcpLockAt extraction.

routing.reasoning: Four bounded runtime edits reuse existing lock validation, serialization, provider and CLI patterns without a new service abstraction; strict isolated TDD remains mandatory because fallback changes tool admission and must fail closed.

suggestedCriteria: buildMcpRollup preserves the lockSource of every supplied withheld entry unchanged.
nax mcp lock without --global still writes only the project lock and prints its project path.
createMcpProviders without a readLock override withholds all advertised tools when a malformed project lock exists, even if the global lock pins those tools.

modifiedFiles.reason: the withheld assertion at `:97` uses `toEqual([{ serverId, name, reason }])`; US-002 adds the required `lockSource` field to `McpWithheldEntry`, and the test's `readLock` stub returns a bare `McpLockFile`, so the entry now carries `lockSource: "project"`. Replacing invariant: the same entry plus `lockSource: "project"`.
the `mcp lock` command gains `.option("--global", ...)` and passes `{ global: options.global === true }` to `runMcpLockCommand`; `runTrustGate` is unchanged.
`writeMcpLock`'s body moves into the new `writeMcpLockAt(path, lock)`; `writeMcpLock(projectRoot, lock)` keeps its signature and output.

the `withheld` literals at `:18` and `:45` are typed `McpWithheldEntry` and lack the new required `lockSource` field, which fails typecheck. Replacing invariant: each literal gains `lockSource: "project"`; the rollup still passes `withheld` through unchanged.

userStories.title: Blocking execution.preRun steps
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] NaxConfigSchema.parse({}) yields execution.preRun equal to [].
[unit] A config with execution.preRun: [{ command: "true" }] parses to a step whose timeoutSeconds is 300.
[unit] A config with execution.preRun: [{ command: "" }] fails schema validation.
[unit] A config with a pre-run step whose timeoutSeconds is 0, -1 or 1.5 fails schema validation.
[unit] runPreRunSteps calls _preRunDeps.executeWithTimeout once per step, in configured order, each with { cwd: workdir } and the step's timeoutSeconds.
[unit] runPreRunSteps throws a NaxError with code PRE_RUN_FAILED and a message containing the command and exit 3 when a step's result is success: false, timeout: false, exitCode: 3.
[unit] runPreRunSteps throws PRE_RUN_FAILED with a message containing exit unknown when a failing step's result has no exitCode.
[unit] runPreRunSteps does not call executeWithTimeout for a second step after the first step fails.
[unit] runPreRunSteps throws PRE_RUN_FAILED with a message containing timed out after 5s when a step with timeoutSeconds: 5 returns success: false, timeout: true.
[unit] runPreRunSteps calls _preRunDeps.assertTrusted(workdir, "pre-run") before executeWithTimeout.
[unit] When assertTrusted throws PROJECT_UNTRUSTED, runPreRunSteps propagates that error without calling executeWithTimeout.
[unit] runPreRunSteps logs Pre-run step completed at info with storyId: "_run" as the first data key, plus command, exitCode and durationMs, for a successful step.
[unit] runPreRunSteps logs Pre-run step failed at error with storyId: "_run" first, plus command, exitCode, timedOut and outputTail, for a failing step.
[unit] runPreRunSteps({ steps: [], workdir }) resolves without calling assertTrusted or executeWithTimeout.
[integration] runExecutionPhase with execution.preRun: [{ command: "up" }] invokes the stubbed _preRunDeps.executeWithTimeout before _captureDeps.writeRunBaseline (recorded call order).
[integration] runExecutionPhase with a pre-run step whose stubbed result is success: false rejects with PRE_RUN_FAILED.
[integration] In that failing case, _captureDeps.writeRunBaseline is never called.
[integration] In that failing case, _unifiedExecutorDeps.runIteration is never called.
[integration] In that failing case, statusWriter.setRunStatus is called with "failed".
[integration] runExecutionPhase with dryRun: true and a configured pre-run step never calls _preRunDeps.executeWithTimeout.
[unit] runPreRunSteps throws PRE_RUN_FAILED with context { stage: "execution", command, exitCode } when a step exits non-zero.
[unit] runPreRunSteps throws PRE_RUN_FAILED with context { stage: "execution", command, exitCode } when a step times out.
[integration] runExecutionPhase sets run status to "failed" when the pre-run trust check throws PROJECT_UNTRUSTED.
[integration] runExecutionPhase awaits statusWriter.update(0, 0) after setting failed and before propagating a pre-run failure.
[unit] runPreRunSteps does not retry a failed or timed-out step.

[integration] runExecutionPhase with execution.preRun: [], dryRun: false and a pending story still calls _captureDeps.writeRunBaseline before the first _unifiedExecutorDeps.runIteration, preserving the existing baseline-before-dispatch order.

routing.reasoning: Seven schema/type/trust/lifecycle touchpoints must agree on defaults and place fail-closed setup before the existing nonblocking baseline; strict isolated TDD is required for unsandboxed host execution and trust refusal.

suggestedCriteria: runPreRunSteps logs a timed-out step at error in stage execution with storyId: "_run" first, timedOut: true, timeoutSeconds, durationMs and outputTail.
runPreRunSteps logs only the last 2000 output characters as outputTail when a failing command produces more than 2000 characters.
A resumed run invokes all configured preRun steps again before baseline capture.
runExecutionPhase with PROJECT_UNTRUSTED from a pre-run trust check never captures a baseline or dispatches a story.

modifiedFiles.reason: declares `PreRunStepConfig { readonly command: string; readonly timeoutSeconds: number }`.

the hand-written `ExecutionConfig` gains a one-line `preRun: PreRunStepConfig[];` field (no doc comment) and `PreRunStepConfig` joins the existing import from the sibling runtime-types-execution module; the file is at 595 of 600 lines, so nothing else is added.

the outer `NaxConfigSchema` `execution` default literal must include `preRun: []` (BUG-20: zod does not re-parse a `.default()` value, so omitting it leaves `execution.preRun` undefined under `NaxConfigSchema.parse({})`).

userStories.title: nax cost command
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose the US-004 ledger query through an independently registered, injectable nax cost CLI with table and JSON reports.

**Motivation** — `nax status --cost` reads one project's `metrics.json`, has no time window, no token split, no grouping, and cannot separate provider-reported (`confidence: "exact"`) from catalog-estimated cost.

**Approach** — Part D — `nax cost` (US-004, US-005)

### Approach

Pure read of the JSONL ledger; no LLM call, no writes. Core in a new `src/cli/cost-ledger-query.ts` (US-004); the command in a new `src/cli/cost.ts` (US-005), registered from `bin/nax.ts` with `registerCostCommand(program)` — the same shape as `registerGatesCommand` (`src/cli/gates.ts:336`, deps seam `_gatesCliDeps`).

**Interface** — CLI deps seam (US-005)

```typescript
export interface CostCliDeps {
  log: (msg: string) => void;        // stdout
  logErr: (msg: string) => void;     // stderr
  exit: (code: number) => void;
  now: () => number;                 // epoch ms
  globalConfigDir: () => string;
  /** Output dir of the project at `dir`: projectOutputDir(config.name?.trim() || basename(dir), config.outputDir), config from loadConfig(dir) (re-implemented in cost.ts; status-cost's resolveProject is private). Like status-cost, a loadConfig failure falls back to projectOutputDir(basename(dir), undefined). */
  resolveProjectOutputDir: (dir: string) => Promise<string>;
  listProjectOutputDirs: typeof listProjectOutputDirs;
  listCostLedgerFiles: typeof listCostLedgerFiles;
  queryCostLedger: typeof queryCostLedger;
}
export const _costCliDeps: CostCliDeps; // real process.stdout/stderr/exit, Date.now, and the US-004 functions
export function registerCostCommand(program: Command, deps?: CostCliDeps): Command; // deps defaults to _costCliDeps
```

Usage errors (`COST_USAGE` from `resolveCostWindow`, or an unknown `--by` key) and any error thrown by `listProjectOutputDirs`, `listCostLedgerFiles`, `queryCostLedger` or `resolveProjectOutputDir` go to `deps.logErr` as `Error: <message>`, followed by `deps.exit(1)`. Success ends with `deps.exit(0)`. `--here` and `--project` combine: `--here` picks the root, and `--project` still filters rows.

### CLI Behavior (US-005)

```
nax cost [--today] [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--until YYYY-MM-DD] [--utc]
         [--by <key[,key...]>] [--project <name>] [--here] [--feature <name>] [--run <runId>]
         [--json] [-d, --dir <path>]
```

- Scan roots: by default every directory returned by `deps.listProjectOutputDirs(deps.globalConfigDir())`. `--here` replaces that with the single root `deps.resolveProjectOutputDir(dir)`. `--project <name>` filters rows by `projectKey` (it does not change the roots).
- `--by` accepts a comma list of `CostGroupKey`; an unknown key is a usage error.
- stdout, default: a fixed-width table — one column per group key, then `calls`, `runs`, `input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, `costUsd`; one line per group; a final `TOTAL` line; then `exact $<exactUsd> / estimated $<estimatedUsd>`; then `skipped <skippedRows> unparseable row(s)` only when `skippedRows > 0`. Dollar amounts to 2 decimals.
- stdout, `--json`: exactly one JSON document, the `CostLedgerReport`.
- stderr: usage errors as `Error: <message>`.
- Exit 0: report produced (including an empty report with zero rows). Exit 1: usage error (`COST_USAGE`) or a read failure.

```
$ nax cost --today --by stage
stage      calls  runs  input     output   cacheRead   cacheWrite  costUsd
run          240    28  30123456  4800000  900000000   2000000     45.10
review        50    12   7000000   900000  150000000    400000     12.20
plan           8     4   1676544   260000   30000000     80000      3.10
TOTAL        298    32  38800000  5960000  1080000000  2480000     60.40
exact $18.74 / estimated $41.66
```

Upstream contract consumed from US-004: CostGroupKey is `"model" | "stage" | "role" | "project" | "feature" | "run" | "story"`; resolveCostWindow takes `{ today?, since?, until?, utc?, nowMs }` and returns inclusive sinceMs/exclusive untilMs. Today is local midnight (UTC under --utc) with no upper bound; until includes its entire named calendar day. Today combined with since/until and invalid calendar dates throw COST_USAGE. An until earlier than since is allowed and yields zero rows. queryCostLedger takes files plus `{ sinceMs?, untilMs?, projects?, feature?, runId?, groupBy }` and returns the schemaVersion 1 CostLedgerReport. JSON output is one compact line, not a logger record or a metrics report.

**Scope** — In: new cost.ts containing registerCostCommand, costCommand and _costCliDeps, real project-output resolution with config failure fallback, rendering, CLI barrel export, bin registration next to registerGatesCommand and tests through program.parseAsync (SEAM-1). Keep the spec's missing-ledger-file query criterion in this story even though it exercises the upstream core. Out: implementation of the US-004 discovery/query/window algorithms; US-001 through US-003. `nax status --cost` is unchanged; `nax cost` is a separate command. `nax cost` does not discover projects whose `outputDir` points outside the global config dir unless `--here` is used from that project. `nax cost` performs no budget checks, alerts, writes, or LLM calls. `nax cost` does not validate duplicate `--by` keys. `nax cost` counts `runs` and groups `run` / `story` by the raw `runId` / `storyId` values, without qualifying them by project; ids that collide across projects are merged. Failed-dispatch ledger rows carry no `featureName`, so `nax cost --feature <name>` excludes them; attributing failed spend to a feature is not added.

analysis:
Feature scope: close #2319, #2408, #2521 and #2595 with five implementation stories, all scoped to packages/nax. This is an enhancement of an existing Bun/TypeScript CLI, not a greenfield application. The codebase-memory MCP tools were unavailable, so discovery used direct source reads and text searches. No implementation or test execution was performed while drafting.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:7 indexes the focused conventions; :157 documents the source/type-only 600-line hard limits, function limits, injected external dependencies, structured errors, barrel boundaries and cancellable subprocess cleanup. Use bun:test, the existing @test/helpers builders, named constants and injectable _deps seams. New modules remain inside nax; no dependency or package-boundary changes are needed. Do not import nax-ai or introduce LLM calls. All contextFiles and expectedFiles are repository-root-relative despite story workdir being packages/nax. Test additions belong to their implementation story. Run package-scoped targeted tests with a path and timeout, never bare bun test; validation gates are pipeline work, not acceptance criteria.

US-001 existing behavior and impact: packages/nax/src/cli/features-acceptance.ts:37 defines the three-value status; :56 implements the never-throw resolver. Its existing order is project discovery (:64), loadConfig (:70), acceptance.enabled (:71), PRD existence (:76), PRD/group resolution (:81), then a catch (:108) that currently logs a warning and falsely returns no-prd (:116). Preserve that order, last-known enabled value, logger warning, per-package command resolution (:125), and no-throw contract; only caught failures gain status error and structured NaxError.code/errorMessage data. packages/nax/src/errors.ts:7 re-exports the canonical NaxError, so use that identity for instanceof rather than duck-typing an arbitrary code property. packages/nax/src/cli/features-resolve.ts:58 silently omits testPatterns on loadConfig failure; :156 exports resolveFeatureSpec. Both its named-feature success path (:204-212) and single auto-discovered-feature success path (:258-267) call acceptance/test-pattern resolution and need the same once-computed override. Explicit Markdown paths currently have featureName null (:189-197); do not invent PRD/profile adoption for those. Reuse packages/nax/src/cli/resolve-run-profile.ts:21 unchanged: CLI chain wins (:31), an environment profile suppresses PRD adoption (:33), and a PRD chain is adopted only when every non-default name exists (:44-56). Important nuance: the helper returns undefined when an env profile is present; packages/nax/src/config/loader.ts:305-310 then reads process.env.NAX_PROFILE itself. Do not convert undefined into an empty CLI override that masks loader precedence. loadConfig(startDir, cliOverrides) is already supported at loader.ts:294, with overlays before schema validation (:331-354). featureDir(root, name) is exported at packages/nax/src/config/paths/index.ts:119; alias an import if needed because features-resolve.ts:218 currently has a local featureDir variable. packages/nax/bin/nax.ts:139 collects repeated profile flags; :614-662 registers features resolve and bases exit codes solely on the top-level result. Add the option and optional third argument without changing that contract. packages/nax/src/cli/index.ts:63-70 exports the acceptance types and resolvers; expose the new error type consistently. Existing two-argument consumers remain source-compatible: packages/nax/src/cli/spec-lint-command.ts:102, advisor-replay.ts:88, workflow/step-context.ts:64-65 and finish/context.ts:250. No changes to those flows are required. packages/nax/src/finish/route.ts:37-40 already treats zero acceptance groups as unverified; error groups must stay empty and finish routing is not redesigned. Regression anchors: packages/nax/test/unit/cli/features-acceptance.test.ts:106 and :118 pin the old malformed-PRD/invalid-config no-prd behavior and must be replaced, not left contradictory. Existing features-resolve.test.ts covers discovery, spec paths, validation and testPatterns. Use pipeline-mode invalid-config fixtures so workflow normalization does not hide execution.storyIsolation validation; initRepo at features-acceptance.test.ts:22 already follows that convention. Isolate NAX_PROFILE/global-config environment changes and restore them. No data migration; callers receive an additive optional error object and a widened status union.

US-002 existing behavior and security boundary: packages/nax/src/mcp/lock.ts:47 reads only a project lock, validates version/servers and returns undefined for missing or malformed data; :61 sorts and serializes exactly version and servers. Preserve readMcpLock's public project-only semantics and validation while factoring path-based reading/writing internally. New resolution must distinguish presence from successful parsing: an existing malformed project lock must not fall back to global. packages/nax/src/config/paths/index.ts:63 reads NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR dynamically, so globalMcpLockPath must honor tests' isolated temp directory. packages/nax/src/mcp/provider.ts:24 defines required withheld fields; :37 provides the bare-McpLockFile read seam; :46 selects the reader and :49-50 memoizes one lock read per provider set. Keep that seam and memoization, derive source without requiring test stubs to change return types, and carry lockSource into callback entries (:84-85) and the existing warn data (:89-96). AllowedTools still only narrows locked tools (:100-101); tool closures keep the hop workdir, not the runtime root (:109-111). packages/nax/src/mcp/rollup.ts:56 passes withheld through unchanged and runtime/index.ts:393 collects McpWithheldEntry values, so source attribution reaches the rollup without a second transformation. packages/nax/src/mcp/index.ts:3 already exports all lock exports. packages/nax/src/cli/mcp.ts:17 loads the same config and lists every enabled server; :26-39 closes its pool in finally. Retain listing and cleanup while selecting project/global destination. packages/nax/bin/nax.ts:992-999 gates trust before invoking the lock command; --global must not bypass or change that gate. Tests to extend: test/unit/mcp/lock.test.ts, provider.test.ts and rollup.test.ts; provider.test.ts:97 expects an exact entry without lockSource and must gain project, and rollup.test.ts:18/:45 literals need the required field. Exercise the actual default provider reader without readLock injection, plus the existing test/fixtures/mcp/fake-server.ts for command integration. The new fallback changes admission for projects lacking a lock, so classify this as access-control/security-sensitive and use strict three-session TDD. Migration is opt-in global lock creation; existing project locks and serialized bytes retain precedence and shape. No server-by-server merge, server-origin verification or trust weakening.

US-003 execution lifecycle and risk: packages/nax/src/execution/runner-execution.ts:87 is the shared runExecutionPhase; :115-119 initially writes running status, :139-158 creates new package directories under a warn-and-continue guard, and :175-189 captures the baseline under another warn-and-continue guard. Insert the new awaited, dry-run-guarded setup between those existing blocks, before routing/dispatch (:192 onward). A pre-run rejection must never enter either neighbor's continue-on-error handler: the execution-phase error boundary must set failed, await update(0, 0), then rethrow the original failure. Preserve baseline's nonblocking contract and make only setup fail-closed. The runner calls this phase at packages/nax/src/execution/runner.ts:315; both workflow and classic dispatch share this entry. Resume intentionally runs setup again; no persistent completion flag or retry loop. packages/nax/src/verification/executor.ts:102-115 exposes executeWithTimeout with cwd and optional environment/options; :120 checks test-command trust and :126-135 spawns /bin/sh -c with process-group cleanup. Reuse it, do not build another shell/process runner or agent operation. packages/nax/src/trust/registry.ts:43 performs async realpath-normalized checks; :65-71 throws PROJECT_UNTRUSTED with surface context. Add pre-run to packages/nax/src/trust/types.ts:53 and explicitly check it before executeWithTimeout so refusal names the intended surface. These host-side arbitrary commands are trust/access-control sensitive: strict three-session TDD is mandatory. Config additions span schemas-execution.ts (ExecutionConfigSchema; worktree neighbor at :318), schemas.ts:155 outer execution default, runtime-types-execution.ts:18 adjacent subtype, and runtime-types.ts:14-21 import/:164 execution field area. runtime-types.ts has exactly 595 lines as read, so only add the imported name and one-line preRun field, no comment or unrelated reformat. Zod does not reparse the outer default: schemas-execution.ts:344-353 explains BUG-20; ensure both an omitted execution object and a partial execution object yield preRun defaults. Default [] keeps all existing runs unchanged; step timeout resolves to 300. Test runner ordering and failed status via test/unit/execution/runner-execution-capture.test.ts:31 makeOptions and its _captureDeps/_unifiedExecutorDeps seams, and test actual trust refusal with no spawn. Stub timing, logging and execution and restore all deps. Results are log-only; do not extend metrics, summary, hook behavior or per-package setup.

US-004 ledger model and query architecture: packages/nax/src/runtime/cost-aggregator.ts:3 defines CostEvent with ts/runId/projectKey, sessionRole (:45), featureName (:46), optional tokens (:60), cost/confidence (:87-90) and partial (:14). CostErrorEvent starts at :148, has optional tokens/exactCostUsd/costUsd (:175-191), no confidence and no featureName. Read JSONL as unknown and validate the specified minimum shape rather than coercing every line to the successful-event interface; legacy rows must remain countable. Validate row ts and present costUsd before time/project filters so invalid rows count as skipped even outside the requested window. Missing costs/tokens are zero, blank lines are ignored, error and partial rows count normally, error rows additionally increment errorCalls, and error exactness depends on finite exactCostUsd while dollars still come from costUsd. Use the directory-derived project fallback consistently for filters and groups. Grouping uses ordered group keys, mapped row fields and a collision-safe composite key; each total/group tracks its own distinct raw runIds. Do not qualify ids by project or deduplicate partial rows. Preserve costUsd = exactUsd + estimatedUsd, with descending group cost ordering. packages/nax/src/runtime/paths.ts:18 derives output directories from globalConfigDir, absolute overrides or ~/ overrides and throws for relative overrides (:29-32); it does not discover external outputs. New filesystem discovery is shallow and sorted; stat children rather than relying exclusively on Dirent.isDirectory so symlinks count. Distinguish ENOENT from other filesystem errors; ledger file reads must propagate even if a previously listed file vanishes. Date-only parsing must validate real dates and construct local or UTC calendar boundaries; adding a local calendar day must not assume every day has 24 hours. No time zone flag beyond --utc, no writes or LLMs. Existing test/unit/runtime/cost-aggregator*.test.ts protect producers, which must stay unchanged; new query tests use temporary JSONL files, malformed/legacy/error/partial fixtures, time endpoints and deterministic nowMs. This is a bounded standard read/query module, not a new service. Its API is the only producer dependency for US-005.

US-005 command integration: packages/nax/src/cli/gates.ts:336 demonstrates registerGatesCommand returning the registered Command with injected deps, and :322-329 demonstrates guarded action/exit behavior; :331-335 explains why commands promising one JSON document must not initialize a stdout logger. packages/nax/test/unit/cli/gates.test.ts:78-125 records stdout/stderr/exit and uses Commander parseAsync; mirror that pattern rather than testing only a detached action. New cost.ts consumes US-004's exported functions with exactly the specified CostCliDeps seam. packages/nax/src/cli/status-cost.ts:15-19 has a private resolveProject: duplicate its small config/name/basename/outputDir rule locally as required, including config-load fallback, rather than exporting it or changing status --cost. Default discovery must not load the current project; --here resolves one project output dir, and --project still filters rows even under --here. Invalid windows and unknown group keys must produce Error: on stderr and exit 1 with no success exit; discovery/query/output-dir read errors do likewise. JSON is compact one-line schemaVersion 1 with no diagnostics on stdout; text output always includes TOTAL, exact/estimated split and only a nonzero skipped-row line. Dollar cells are fixed to two decimals and columns align by actual rendered widths. Register next to registerGatesCommand at packages/nax/bin/nax.ts:986 via the cli barrel (packages/nax/src/cli/index.ts:71-79). Preserve all existing status-cost reports and exit semantics. Place the spec's queryCostLedger-missing-file criterion under US-005 even though it exercises the upstream core; do not move it to US-004. Test seam wiring through parseAsync and a real bin command for output isolation.

Execution and migration plan: US-001, US-002, US-003 and US-004 have no story dependencies; US-005 depends only on US-004. US-001/US-002/US-005 edit different registrations in the same bin/nax.ts, and US-001/US-005 both touch the cli barrel; reconcile these additive hunks if executed in parallel without adding dependency edges. There are no storage/schema migrations, new package dependencies, release bumps or cross-package edits. Compatibility changes are intentional: acceptance catches become error rather than no-prd; MCP withholding records gain required lockSource; absent project locks may use an operator-created global lock; configured preRun now blocks execution while default [] remains a no-op; cost is wholly additive. outOfScope: Updating `docs/guides/configuration.md`, `docs/guides/mcp-and-interception.md` and a guide page for `nax cost` is a manual follow-up after this feature merges; no story edits docs.
